stage_a.note: Strong enthusiastic delivery, especially when introducing the mascot.
Animated gestures and engaged excitement while explaining the product.
Frequent smiles and approachable, friendly orientation toward the panel.

venture.description: Gourmet, bite-sized frozen pizza snacks shaped like cupcakes with a hybrid brioche and sourdough crust.
venture.note: They sell direct to consumers online and also cater to stadiums like Citi Field.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle and Andrea introduce themselves and state their ask of 125k for 5 percent.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea asks who does not love pizza and notes that pizza lovers are all over the world.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle explains that frozen pizza is usually not seen as a gourmet snack and the category has gone stale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders enthusiastically introduce their mascot, the Pizza Cupcake, who dances for the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea describes the product as the next level of pizza made with high quality ingredients and a secret dough.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle highlights the cupcake shape, making it perfect for any occasion, and invites the panel to taste.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert tells the founders to stop talking so the panel can eat the cupcakes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle encourages the investors to dig in and taste the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea points out the Margherita and Pepperoni flavors available for the investors to try.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement at the taste of the cupcakes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if the marinara sauce is their own recipe.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea confirms that the marinara sauce is their own creation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond remarks that the cupcake is delicious.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark praises the taste and jokes that he hates them because he wants to keep eating.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea explains that the product is a hybrid rather than a regular pizza.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks why it is so good and compares the texture to a flaky pastry.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea confirms the texture and states that they use only olive oil, with no butter.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks for confirmation that there is no butter in the recipe.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea confirms it uses only olive oil and describes the dough as a hybrid between brioche and sourdough.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks how old the sample is, noting it tastes like it was made that morning.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea clarifies that the product they are eating is actually frozen.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks if they ship the frozen cupcakes from New York.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle confirms that they ship the product from New York.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark states that the marinara flavor is his favorite.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori jokes that it is amazing to see Kevin silent and just eating.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert agrees that the cupcakes are very good.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle mentions that the Margherita cupcake has 160 calories.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks if that calorie count is for a single cupcake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle confirms that the 160 calories are for one piece.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea adds that the pepperoni flavor has 170 calories per piece.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks Andrea to share his background and how he came up with the recipe.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea shares his background growing up in Venice, working as a chef, and moving to London and New York.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks how Andrea and Michelle met.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle explains they met through a mutual friend and Andrea took her on a pizza date.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert jokes that he is sure Andrea did that.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea jokes back that he had to show off his skills.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle adds that they have been married for almost two years and this business is their first baby.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark congratulates the couple on their business and marriage.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle shares her background as an event producer working with influencers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks how they transitioned from having a product to launching a business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea explains that after serving it at a friend's event, the positive reaction prompted Michelle to bring it to her events.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks about their current sales channels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle explains they sell direct to consumer and previously sold through catering, Smorgasburg, and stadiums like Citi Field.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they use a commercial kitchen for production.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle confirms they use a commercial kitchen and have worked with a co-packer for the last nine months.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their projected sales are for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle states they are projecting 800k in sales for the year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle adds that they did 344k last year and have done 77k year to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle explains that prior to Covid they were a restaurant business and had to pivot to e-commerce.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks for confirmation that they sell a frozen product direct to customers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle confirms they sell direct to customers because people wanted to know where to find them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin challenges the viability of shipping frozen products, noting the high cost of weight based on his past experience.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle responds that their goal is to find additional fulfillment centers to reduce shipping costs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks what they charge for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle answers that a 12-pack costs 24.99.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks how much they charge for shipping.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea states that shipping costs 9.99.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert clarifies that the total cost is 35 dollars for 12 pieces.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle confirms Robert's calculation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark notes that the price breaks down to about three dollars per cupcake.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks what it costs them to make each cupcake.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea answers that it currently costs 95 cents to make one cupcake.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark challenges the production cost, stating that it is expensive.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea explains the cost is high due to handmade production, but their recipe allows scaling down to 48 cents.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle adds that they are seeking investment to start production with their co-packer and lower costs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin exits, citing the significant challenges of starting up and figuring out frozen shipping.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond exits, feeling he would not be the best partner as his expertise lies in a different category.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert exits, stating he is torn but believes they will get a better offer than he would make.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori offers 125k for 20 percent, noting the great synergy with her other investment, Bantam Bagels.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori reiterates her offer of 125k for 20 percent to the founders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle argues that the value they bring to the table makes them worth more than the offer implies.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that Lori's offer sounds like a mob offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori defends her offer, stating she could have asked for an even higher equity percentage.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori emphasizes that they can follow in the successful distribution footsteps of Bantam Bagels.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, advising that if they want to stay frozen, partnering with Lori and Bantam is the best route.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle counters Lori's offer, asking if she would be willing to do 125k for 10 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori revises her offer to 125k for 15 percent, refusing to go down to 10 percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle counters again, asking if Lori would do 125k for 12.5 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori holds firm at 15 percent, expressing her strong desire to be invested in them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle counters by asking for a higher amount, 150k for 15 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori rejects the higher amount, restating her offer of 125k for 15 percent.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Andrea points out that Bantam Bagels received a higher valuation when they were on the show.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle adds that they have higher revenue than Bantam did and have already secured a co-packer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori argues that her experience can save them two years of mistakes, justifying her equity ask.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin warns the founders that they are skating on thin ice by negotiating so hard with their only offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle makes a final counter of 125k for 12.5 percent equity plus 2.5 percent in advisory shares.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori accepts the founders' counter offer, securing the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michelle and Andrea excitedly accept the deal and thank Lori.

decisions.note: Shipping frozen is hard, starting up challenges.
Not the best partner, different category.
Will get a better offer, torn.
Getting space is hard, Bantam is a better partner.
20% is too high, have made progress.
Will not go to 10%, bottom line is 15%.
